extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and practitioners (design patent applicants and attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination and prosecution of U.S. design patent applications, focusing on restriction practice, grouping of embodiments, drawing requirements, and related procedural requirements (elections, traverses, telephone provisional elections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple embodiments in one application only if patentably indistinct
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple embodiments of a single inventive concept may be included in the same design application only if they are patentably indistinct. See In re Rubinfield, 270 F.2d 391, 123 USPQ 210 (CCPA 1959).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embodiments that are patentably distinct from one another do not constitute a single inventive concept and thus may not be included in the same design application. See In re Platner, 155 USPQ 222 (Comm’r Pat. 1967). If embodiments are deemed to comprise a single inventive concept, no argument asserting patentability based on differences between those embodiments will be considered once that determination is made; failure to traverse is an admission of lack of patentable distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping criterion — obvious variations / patentably indistinct within group
rubrics_metrics.description: The embodiments disclosed within each group have overall appearances that are basically the same; the differences between them are considered minor and patentably indistinct, or are shown to be obvious in view of analogous prior art cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such embodiments are considered obvious variations of one another within the group, comprise a single inventive concept, and may be retained and examined in the same application. Any rejection of one embodiment over prior art will apply equally to all other embodiments in the group. Examiner should identify groups and note why embodiments are grouped; applicant cannot rely on differences between embodiments in the same group to support patentability once grouped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groups must be patentably distinct from each other to avoid restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of the differences identified, the embodiments of each group are considered to either have overall appearances that are not basically the same, or, if they are basically the same, the differences are not minor and patentably indistinct or are not shown to be obvious in view of analogous prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When groups are patentably distinct, restriction is required under 35 U.S.C. 121 to one of the patentably distinct groups of designs. Examiner must insert explanations of differences between the groups and list group membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction requirement and required election
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to this requirement must include an election of a single group for prosecution on the merits, even if this requirement is traversed, 37 CFR 1.143.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reply that does not include election of a single group will be held nonresponsive. Applicant is also requested to direct cancellation of all drawing figures and the corresponding descriptions which are directed to the nonelected groups. If applicant traverses, they should present evidence now of record showing groups to be obvious variations of one another; otherwise any rejection of one group will apply equally to others. Action on the merits is deferred pending compliance with the requirement (see Ex parte Heckman).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when applicant traverses restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Should applicant traverse this requirement on the grounds that the groups are not patentably distinct, applicant should present evidence or identify such evidence now of record showing the groups to be obvious variations of one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If groups are determined not to be patentably distinct and they remain in this application, any rejection of one group over prior art will apply equally to all other groups. No argument asserting patentability based on differences between the groups will be considered once the groups have been determined to comprise a single inventive concept. Failure to traverse is an admission of lack of patentable distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone provisional election and affirmation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: During a telephone discussion a provisional election may be made to prosecute a particular group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirmation of any provisional telephone election should be made by applicant in replying to the Office action. Group(s) not elected are withdrawn from further consideration by the examiner under 37 CFR 1.142(b). Examiner notes should be used to record provisional elections made by telephone (insert --with-- or --without-- as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction for segregable parts / combination-subcombination
rubrics_metrics.description: Designs which involve a change in scope or patentably distinct segregable parts may not be included in the same design application; design protection does not extend to patentably distinct segregable parts of a design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combination/subcombination subject matter, if patentably distinct, must be supported by separate claims, whereas only a single claim is permissible in a design patent application. The only way to protect patentably distinct segregable parts is to apply for separate patents. Restriction to one of the inventions is required under 35 U.S.C. 121 in such situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common embodiment included in multiple groups — qualifying statement and double patenting caution
rubrics_metrics.description: The common embodiment is included in more than a single group as it is patentably indistinct from the other embodiment(s) in those groups and to give applicant the broadest possible choices in his or her election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the common embodiment is elected in this application, applicant is advised that the common embodiment should not be included in any continuing application to avoid a rejection on the ground of double patenting under 35 U.S.C. 171 in the new application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent subject matter — ornamental appearance only
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention is directed to the fact that design patent applications are concerned solely with the ornamental appearance of an article of manufacture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The functional and/or structural features stressed by applicant in the papers are of no concern in design cases, and are neither permitted nor required. Function and structure fall under the realm of utility patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual characteristics as the basis of design
rubrics_metrics.description: The design for an article consists of the visual characteristics or aspect displayed by the article; it is the appearance presented by the article which creates an impression through the eye upon the mind of the observer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject matter of a design patent may relate to the configuration or shape of an article, to the surface ornamentation on an article, or to both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design inseparable from article — definiteness and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Design is inseparable from the article to which it is applied, and cannot exist alone merely as a scheme of ornamentation. It must be a definite preconceived thing, capable of reproduction, and not merely the chance result of a method or of a combination of functional elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 35 U.S.C. 171; 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and (b). Insufficient definition or inability to reproduce the design may be problematic for entitlement and validity (see Blisscraft v. United Plastics and related authority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impermissible descriptive statement in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The descriptive statement included in the specification is impermissible because [reason].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a general rule, the illustration in the drawing views is its own best description; any description of the design in the specification, other than a brief description of the drawing, is generally not necessary and should be canceled. (See MPEP § 1503.01, subsection II.) Examiner should insert the reason why the descriptive statement is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic feature statement — permissibility and caution
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'characteristic features' statement describing a particular feature of novelty or nonobviousness in the claimed design may be permissible in the specification (e.g., 'The characteristic feature of the design resides in [1]').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While permissible, the patentability of the claimed design is not based on the specified feature but rather on a comparison of the overall appearance of the design with the prior art. Use of a characteristic feature statement may later serve to limit the claim. Examiner notes should ask for brief but accurate descriptions of the feature of novelty or nonobviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity for good drawings — drawings as whole disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The necessity for good drawings in a design patent application cannot be overemphasized. As the drawing constitutes the whole disclosure of the design, it is of utmost importance that it be so well executed both as to clarity of showing and completeness, that nothing regarding the design sought to be patented is left to conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An insufficient drawing may be fatal to validity (35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph) and may negatively affect the effective filing date of a continuing application. Examiner should ensure drawings fully disclose claimed design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of broken lines for indicating unimportant features not permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The ornamental design which is being claimed must be shown in solid lines in the drawing. Broken lines for the purpose of indicating unimportant or immaterial features of the design are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no portions of a claimed design which are immaterial or unimportant. See In re Blum and In re Zahn. Where environmental structure is illustrated, broken lines may be used only if clearly designated as environment in the specification (see 37 CFR 1.152 and MPEP § 1503.02, subsection III), and a statement describing the broken lines must be inserted in the specification. Do not use environmental-broken-line paragraphs in international design applications. If superimposed broken lines obscure full-line disclosure, a separate figure showing the broken lines must be included in addition to figures showing only claimed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of broken lines — required statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement similar to: 'The broken line showing of [1] is for the purpose of illustrating [2] and forms no part of the claimed design.' should be used to describe the broken lines on the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert such a statement in the specification preceding the claim. In bracketed form paragraphs, specify the name of the structure and whether the broken lines illustrate 'portions of the "article"' or 'environmental structure', and whether the statement 'must be' or 'has been' inserted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction consequences — withdrawal and cancellation of nonelected groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Group(s) not elected for prosecution are withdrawn from further consideration by the examiner (37 CFR 1.142(b)) and, when appropriate, canceled if application is otherwise in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If election was made without traverse in the reply, the nonelected group(s) may be canceled (¶ 15.37). If restriction requirement maintained as final and applicant traversed, applicant must cancel nonelected group(s) or take other timely appropriate action (37 CFR 1.144). Examiner notes should be used to indicate withdrawn groups and bracketed insertions as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of reply — provisional election needed to complete reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is advised that the reply to be complete must include a provisional election of one of the enumerated designs, even though the requirement may be traversed (37 CFR 1.143).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reply does not include the required election, it may be held nonresponsive and prosecution may be delayed. In telephone-restriction situations, affirmation of provisional elections made during telephone interviews must be made in the written reply.
